claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy lacks a specialized tribolayer.
Applying a nanostructured, temperature-responsive coating will enable in situ formation of an adaptive tribolayer on CoCrFeNi.
The adaptive tribolayer will self-regenerate during sliding.
The coating will maintain low friction and minimal wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
At elevated temperatures, the coating will release beneficial additives that form a lubricious phase.
At lower temperatures, the coating will promote rapid formation of a protective oxide layer.
The coating will alter the surface energy of the CoCrFeNi system.
The coating will catalyze temperature-dependent tribochemical reactions.
Formation of lubricious high-temperature phases and protective low-temperature oxides will ensure steady low-friction and low-wear performance.
The coated alloy will exhibit at least a 25% reduction in coefficient of friction relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The coated alloy will exhibit at least a 25% reduction in wear rate relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits variable and higher friction as operating conditions change.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits variable and higher wear rates as operating conditions change.
The intervention will be effective from room temperature to 800 °C under typical sliding loads and normal atmospheric conditions.
